claim: Heart rate and blood pressure oscillate in phase with respiratory activity.
source: Heart rate and blood pressure oscillate in phase with respiratory activity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known physiological phenomenon that the study investigates.

source: A component of these oscillations is generated centrally, with respiratory neurons entraining the activity of pre-sympathetic and parasympathetic cardiovascular neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as background for the study's investigation.

claim: Excitatory preBötC neurons modulate sympathetic vasomotor neuron activity.

evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract, supported by optogenetic experiments described in the manuscript.

source: generating heart rate and blood pressure oscillations in phase with respiration

claim: Respiratory entrainment of blood pressure is exaggerated in cardiovascular pathologies such as hypertension and heart failure.
source: The findings have implications for cardiovascular pathologies, such as hypertension and heart failure, where respiratory entrainment of heart rate is diminished and respiratory entrainment of blood pressure exaggerated.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as known clinical context for the findings.

source: in heart rate (HR), called respiratory sinus arrhythmia (RSA)

claim: RSA reduces cardiac energetic cost.

claim: Alterations in Traube-Hering waves and RSA contribute to the pathogeneses of hypertension and heart failure.

evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The pathological relevance of Traube-Hering waves and RSA extends to numerous neurological diseases, including depression and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.

claim: Traube-Hering waves are generated by bursts of vasomotor sympathetic nerve activity that occur in phase with the respiratory cycle (RespSNA).
source: Traube-Hering waves are generated by bursts of vasomotor sympathetic nerve activity that occur in phase with the respiratory cycle (RespSNA), spanning most of inspiration and the very beginning of post-inspiration (the first phase of expiration).

claim: RespSNA spans most of inspiration and the very beginning of post-inspiration.
source: Traube-Hering waves are generated by bursts of vasomotor sympathetic nerve activity that occur in phase with the respiratory cycle (RespSNA), spanning most of inspiration and the very beginning of post-inspiration (the first phase of expiration).

claim: Traube-Hering waves peak during post-inspiration as a result of slow vascular contraction dynamics.

claim: RespSNA is the result of respiratory modulation of the activity of pre-sympathetic neurons in the rostral ventrolateral medulla oblongata.
source: RespSNA is the result of respiratory modulation of the activity of pre-sympathetic neurons in the rostral ventrolateral medulla oblongata, and in particular of the excitatory inspiratory modulation of adrenergic C1 neurons (Menuet et al., 2017; Moraes et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: RespSNA is the result of excitatory inspiratory modulation of adrenergic C1 neurons.
source: RespSNA is the result of respiratory modulation of the activity of pre-sympathetic neurons in the rostral ventrolateral medulla oblongata, and in particular of the excitatory inspiratory modulation of adrenergic C1 neurons (Menuet et al., 2017; Moraes et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: RSA is generated by a cardio-inhibitory vagal parasympathetic tone that decreases during the second part of expiration and into inspiration.
source: RSA is generated by a cardio-inhibitory vagal parasympathetic tone that decreases during the second part of expiration and into inspiration, resulting in HR oscillations that peak at the end of inspiration.

claim: HR oscillations in RSA peak at the end of inspiration.
source: RSA is generated by a cardio-inhibitory vagal parasympathetic tone that decreases during the second part of expiration and into inspiration, resulting in HR oscillations that peak at the end of inspiration.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Cardiac vagal preganglionic neurons of the nucleus ambiguus are weakly inhibited during the second part of expiration.
source: Cardiac vagal preganglionic neurons of the nucleus ambiguus are weakly inhibited during the second part of expiration, and strongly inhibited during inspiration, by both GABAergic and glycinergic inputs (Gilbey et al., 1984; Neff et al., 2003).

claim: Cardiac vagal preganglionic neurons of the nucleus ambiguus are strongly inhibited during inspiration by both GABAergic and glycinergic inputs.

evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The specific cellular components of the central respiratory pattern generating circuit responsible for modulation of both vasomotor pre-sympathetic and cardiac vagal preganglionic neurons are not fully elucidated.
source: However, the specific cellular components of the central respiratory pattern generating circuit that are responsible for modulation of both vasomotor pre-sympathetic and cardiac vagal preganglionic neurons are not fully elucidated.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: The preBötC consists of excitatory (glutamatergic) inspiratory neurons, and inhibitory (GABAergic and glycinergic) neurons that can be inspiratory or expiratory.
source: Core to the respiratory column is a small, yet heterogeneous, group of neurons in the preBötzinger Complex (preBötC), which consists of excitatory (glutamatergic) inspiratory neurons, and inhibitory (GABAergic and glycinergic) neurons that can be inspiratory or expiratory (Baertsch et al., 2018; Koizumi et al., 2013; Morgado-Valle et al., 2010; Sherman et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The preBötC is critical for respiratory rhythm generation.
source: The preBötC is critical for respiratory rhythm generation
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: The preBötC acts as a master oscillator entraining the activity of other oscillators, like the sniffing and whisking oscillators, in a unidirectional fashion.
source: and also acts as a master oscillator entraining the activity of other oscillators, like the sniffing and whisking oscillators, in a unidirectional fashion (Deschênes et al., 2016; Moore et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: PreBötC neurons have the anatomical connections to provide the inspiratory input to C1 pre-sympathetic neurons.

source: Prolonged GtACR2-mediated preBötC photoinhibition, either in vivo in anesthetized rats (n = 5) or in the in situ WHBP (n = 12), produced immediate cessation of inspiratory activity and a long-lasting apnea (Figure 2A–C; Figure 3A–C).
